summary.intent: Run the full autonomous post-execution ship pipeline for GSD Phase 68 (web rotation UX / durable anti-rollback client state) — verify, secure, validate, simplify, SDK E2E gate, CodeRabbit review, ship PR, resolve all review threads, and extract learnings — without requiring user babysitting.
summary.outcome: PR #587 was created, all CI checks went green, and multiple rounds of CodeRabbit/Greptile findings were triaged and resolved (fixes pushed across several commits, some findings deferred to documented todos). Several real bugs were found and fixed along the way (crypto zeroization-order bug, NaN/negative bypass in anti-rollback floors, unverified-signature bypass), and the phase's security/validation/learnings docs were committed on the branch; the final merge decision was left to the user.

repo: apps/web vitest is NOT run in CI (only api/crypto/core/sdk-core/sdk/api-client are) — a locally-failing web test isn't necessarily a ship blocker; verify against main before treating it as a regression.
Root `pnpm typecheck` excludes apps/api's own tsc — pre-existing apps/api spec type errors in untouched files aren't caught by the root gate.
sdk-e2e has 11 v1 suites `describe.skip`-quarantined since PR #578 (v2 cutover) alongside 5 live v2 suites — large skip counts there are expected, not a regression.
The TEE lease-renewer stack requires the tee-worker container to be rebuilt from current source before SDK E2E runs, or it serves a stale pre-phase contract (404s on /republish).
docker containers for tee-worker/mock-ipns-routing must be located via container labels when compose file location isn't obvious.
Read plane keying is `ipnsName` alone (no separate node id) per the SealedChildRef contract — CodeRabbit repeatedly flagged this as 'inconsistent keying' but it's by design.
SentShareResponseDto has no plaintext itemName field — a CodeRabbit finding claiming a dropped field was a false positive.

`git filter-branch` / commit reword step is often a no-op in this repo since GSD executor commits already use conventional format with scope-parens (which are valid; only the description part must be paren-free).

code.finding: enumerateMoveDescendants zeroed the parent readKey in a finally block before the children loop finished unsealing with it, misclassifying every depth-2+ move descendant as unreadable — fixed by restructuring try/finally so the key outlives the children walk; covered by a new red-green-verified regression test.

Reconcile gate needed a bigint overflow guard before calling enforceResolved, and enumerateMoveDescendantsFireAndForget needed to zero its own dedicated key copy on both the short-circuit and post-walk paths (separate from the walk's own key).

enforceResolved silently let NaN/negative/fractional generation or seq values bypass the anti-rollback regression check (NaN comparisons are always false); a malformed cold-device versionFloor could also disable the first-contact gate. Fixed with explicit fail-closed validation.

updateGrant needed to be wrapped in a DB transaction with `lock: { mode: 'pessimistic_write' }` on the Share row plus a rootGeneration < existing check throwing ConflictException, to prevent concurrent-update rollback of the anti-rollback floor.

Needed a safeError() helper stripping raw Axios error bodies before logging, a hasSdkClient() re-check after awaiting decodeSentGrants (client could be torn down mid-await), and pagination for the sent-grants fetch (was silently first-page-only, missing reconciles for owners with >50 grants).

workflow: Running long-lived checks (security audit, simplify review, SDK E2E build) as parallel background jobs while orchestrating PR prep in the foreground kept the pipeline moving without idle waiting.
When a background command reports exit code 0, still read the actual output/tail — a masked failure (e.g. a `waitFor timed out` deep in a redirected log) can hide behind a successful process exit.

For CodeRabbit/Greptile PR review resolution: fetch ALL reviewThreads via GraphQL (not just the review body), reply + resolve each individually with a retry wrapper, then re-query to confirm 0 unresolved and no duplicate replies before declaring done.
Greptile re-reviews new push commits, so a 'final' resolved-thread count must be re-swept after any subsequent push before reporting completion.

When a reviewer bot's finding is judged wrong/by-design, replying with the reasoning on the thread (rather than silently dismissing) let Greptile acknowledge and accept it — worth doing before resolving such threads.

friction: Sandboxed Bash silently blocked gh network calls (`dial tcp i/o timeout`), which caused a background poll to compare empty strings and falsely report 'settled' — had to re-run with sandbox disabled to get a real result.
Edit tool repeatedly failed with 'File modified since read' because lint-staged/linters rewrote files during commit — required re-reading and re-applying edits.
zsh quirks: bare `echo ===X===` was interpreted as a command, and cwd persisting into apps/api after a `cd` broke later relative-path commands.

Local TEE stack was misconfigured twice: a stale tee-worker container running a pre-Phase-67 contract, and the API defaulting `TEE_WORKER_URL` to the mock-ipns-routing service port instead of the real tee-worker port — both diagnosed as environment issues, not code regressions, but consumed significant debugging time.

A vitest failure in ipns.service.test.ts required extensive diffing against main (swapping in main's file, checking imports, checking CI job scope) before concluding it was pre-existing and non-blocking.
Session hit its context/usage limit mid-pipeline (during the PR-review poll) and required a 'continue' prompt to resume.
